descriptionChirho: To serve or worship a deity (God or idols) in a religious or covenantal sense; Arabic root ʿ-b-d (عبد) consistently distinguishes this from personal service (kh-d-m) and labor (ʿ-m-l).
To serve or minister to a human master, lord, or king in a personal, relational capacity; Arabic root kh-d-m (خدم) distinguishes this from religious worship (ʿ-b-d) and generic labor (ʿ-m-l).
To work or labor in a general productive sense, not directed at a deity or person; Arabic root ʿ-m-l (عمل) and Korean 일하다 consistently mark this sense; includes compulsory labor contexts.
To till, plow, or cultivate agricultural land; Arabic root f-l-ḥ (فلح) and Korean 경작하다 distinguish this from generic labor; Swahili -lima (to farm) confirms the agricultural specificity.
To cause someone to serve, to enslave or subject to forced labor; Hifil binyan with Arabic استعبد (istaʿbada) or أخضع and Swahili causative -tumikisha marking the causative/coercive dimension.
Niphal passive of the agricultural sense: land being tilled or cultivated; Arabic passive تُفلح and Swahili passive -limwa confirm the passive agricultural meaning.
Qal passive participle indicating something that has been served or worked upon; a rare passive form of the base stem.
Qal active participle used as a substantive noun meaning servant, worshiper, or worker; Arabic عابد (ʿābid) for worshiper contexts, عامل (ʿāmil) for worker contexts; Korean ~하는 자 (one who does).
